page0: my ssd is connected btw use that — clean file struct but everything is meant to be viewed in MOOR applications
objective: Use the connected SSD as durable backing storage for MOOR applications while keeping the filesystem simple, app-owned, and secondary to MOOR's interfaces.

structure.rule: Applications own their backing files. Users primarily view and manipulate the data through MOOR apps rather than by browsing/editing raw files.

mechanism.permission: Browser File System Access API requires one explicit folder selection/permission grant.
mechanism.remembered_handle: Directory handle is remembered in IndexedDB when supported.
mechanism.fallback: Browser-local storage remains a cache/fallback when the SSD is unavailable.
mechanism.migration: Existing local data is merged or migrated into the app-owned SSD file on connection rather than discarded.

done_criteria: One SSD folder selection initializes MOOR/README.txt and MOOR/app-data/.
Quick Notes reads/writes MOOR/app-data/quick-notes/state.json when the remembered SSD handle is available.
Trajectory reads/writes MOOR/app-data/trajectory/local-checkpoints.json and caches canonical history in canonical-cache.json.
MOOR apps remain the primary presentation layer; no raw filesystem UI is introduced.
Browser fallback remains usable if File System Access is unsupported or permission is unavailable.
No app silently claims access to the SSD before the browser grants it.
honest_limits: A normal browser cannot silently take control of an attached drive; the owner must choose the SSD folder once.
The remembered directory handle is browser-profile specific.
This is local durable storage, not automatic cloud sync or cross-device replication.
